This is a QUALITY-CONTROL re-audit of a leadership document, not a first-pass discovery task. A document (Zimmermann_Frontend_Lead_Playbook.md) already makes specific claims about what certain Claude Code skills do, based on earlier research. My job now is to catch any mistakes in those claims, not confirm them — please be skeptical and actively look for ways each claim could be an oversimplification, stale, or outright wrong.

Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/

For each skill below, read its SKILL.md (and, if the SKILL.md references a script it invokes, skim that script too) and verdict the claim as CONFIRMED (matches — cite the exact supporting line/behavior), PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (roughly right but missing real nuance — explain what's missing), or WRONG (doesn't match — explain what's actually true instead).

1. `new-component` → claim: "scaffolds `index.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx` (+ a test if logic-heavy) per conventions.md"
2. `feature-spec` → claim: "one-question-at-a-time clarification, then parallel research agents against the registry/patterns/upstream, then a scoped spec with a ready-to-paste Claude Code prompt"
3. `code-quality` → claim: "read-only audit against conventions.md"
4. `pr-checklist` → claim: "runs code-quality, then classifies every changed file by tier/owner into a PR description"
5. `contentful-register-component` → claim: "generates a component's Contentful Studio definition"
6. `contentful-drift-check` → claim: "audits an existing definition against current props"
7. `scope-check` → claim: "reviews a proposed Claude Code prompt before you run it and verdicts it SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED against the tier system"
8. `onboarding` → claim: "a role-aware, interactive first-day walkthrough"
9. `qa-generate` → claim: turns a Jira user story into a Gherkin `.feature` file; has a two-step gate — Gherkin draft, then **stop for Lead QA sign-off**, only then generate the Playwright spec
10. `upstream-sync-review` → claim: "how you decide whether to bump the PWA Kit dependency without breaking the override surface"
11. `generate-changelog` → claim: "a real, four-audience (dev/QA/product/GitHub Release) reporting tool"
12. `audit-tier` → claim (used narratively, not quoted directly): it can tell a developer whether a specific file is "safe to touch alone" — i.e. it reports per-file tier/ownership/blast-radius info a developer would check before soloing on that file
13. `project-init` → claim (narrative only): does one-time repo setup, asking questions and checking things off, as part of scaffolding/onboarding — confirm this is roughly right, no need for deep detail

This is read-only — do not edit anything. Report back a compact table: skill | verdict | one-line evidence or correction. Flag anything surprising even if not directly asked about (e.g., if a skill does something materially different from its folder name implies).

6	Scaffold a new Zimmermann custom component.

8	The component name is: $ARGUMENTS
9	
10	## Conventions
11	
12	Follow [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) — single source of truth
13	for naming, folder layout, props types, JSDoc policy, and Chakra token usage. Higher-level
14	project rules live in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do not restate rules here — read
15	conventions.md before scaffolding.
16	
17	Key implications for scaffolding:
18	- Component lives in its own folder: `componentName/index.tsx` (Zimmermann-authored) or
19	  `component-name/index.tsx` (override of a base SF component).
20	- Props type named `<ComponentName>Props`, declared at the top of `index.tsx` by default.
21	- Storybook story is mandatory; Vitest only when the component owns non-trivial logic.
22	
23	## Steps
24	
25	1. Read one nearby existing custom component under [overrides/app/components/](../../../overrides/app/components/) to match code style, import order, and Chakra usage. If no Zimmermann-authored component exists yet, read a base template component from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and convert the style to TypeScript + Chakra props.
26	
27	2. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`:
28	   - Functional React component, named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export.
29	   - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.
30	   - JSDoc above the component if it will be consumed by ≥2 callers (shared/Tier 2).
31	   - Chakra primitives for layout (`Box`, `Flex`, `Text`, etc.) using theme tokens — no hardcoded hex, pixel spacing, or raw font sizes.
32	   - No commerce state hooks (`useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`, etc.) — accept data as props; the parent owns data fetching.
33	
34	3. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.stories.tsx` — but first decide
35	   if a story is needed at all. Per [conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) →
36	   **Storybook**, purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent
37	   don't need their own story; cover their variants via the parent. If a story *is* needed:
38	   - Storybook 8.6 CSF3 default export.
39	   - Pick the right category prefix from conventions.md — `Foundation/`, `Primitives/`,
40	     `Commerce/`, `Layout/`, `Forms/`, or `Pages/`. Ask the developer if it's not obvious
41	     which one fits (with your recommendation).
42	   - `title: '<Category>/<ComponentName>'` (e.g. `'Commerce/ProductTile'`,
43	     `'Layout/Header'`).
44	   - At least one named export `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states only —
45	     not every prop combination.
46	   - Add a `play` function only if the component has interactive behaviour worth asserting.
47	
48	4. Optional: if the component owns non-trivial logic, also create `index.test.ts` (Vitest) in the same folder. Skip otherwise.
49	
50	5. Optional: if the props type exceeds ~30 lines or will be consumed by sibling files, move it to `types.ts` in the same folder. Otherwise leave it inline.
51	
52	6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm zero new errors.
53	
54	## Constraints
55	
56	- Do not modify any existing files (no auto-wiring into routes, parents, or the theme registry).
57	- Do not add npm packages — see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 7.
58	- Do not import from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` source directly — re-export from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` paths.
59	- For new icons, use `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`; if a needed icon is missing, ask the developer.
60	
61	## Output
62	
63	Tell the developer:
64	- The paths of every file created.
65	- The import to copy: `import <ComponentName> from '.../components/<componentName>'` (no filename — resolves via `index.tsx`).
66	- A one-sentence note on where it likely wires in, or ask if unsure.
67	- A reminder that `npx tsc --noEmit` was run and passed.

|-----------------------|--------------------------|--------------------|
| string                | Text                     | shortText          |
| string (long/rich)    | Text                     | longText           |
| string union (enum)   | Text                     | select             |
| boolean               | Boolean                  | toggle             |
| number                | Number                   | number             |

| image/media object    | Media                    | — (media field)    |
| href / url string     | Text                     | shortText          |

  these are not content fields. Flag them to the developer.

  name: '[Human Readable Component Name]',

---

Welcome the developer or QA engineer and explain what this skill does in one sentence.

Ask (both roles):

New = full walkthrough. Returning on new machine = focus on mechanical setup, skip orientation.

---

## Phase 2 — Mechanical setup checks

Run these checks inline using the Bash tool. Report results as you go.

```bash
node --version
npm --version
claude --version 2>/dev/null || echo "NOT FOUND"
git branch --show-current
ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg' || echo "hooks missing"
```

For each issue found:

**Hooks missing:**
> "The git hooks aren't installed on this machine. Run both of these now:"
```bash
cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
```
Verify after: `ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'`

**On develop or main:**
> "You're on the `{branch}` branch. You must always work on a feature branch. Create one now:"
```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup
```

**Node too old:** Point to the project's node requirement (24 LTS) and ask them to update before continuing.

**Claude Code not found:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`.

Once all checks pass, say: "Setup is confirmed. Let's cover the rules and tools."

---

*Skip this phase for QA — go to Phase 4.*

Walk through these in order — brief, one at a time, confirm understanding before continuing.

**Branch rule (non-negotiable):**
> "Never work directly on `develop` or `main`. Every task gets a feature branch.
> Before each session: `git branch --show-current`. If it says develop, stop."

**Protection tiers:**
> "Every file in this repo has a tier. Tier 1 = frozen, you cannot touch it without explicit
> owner approval. Tier 2 = protected, requires a second reviewer on the PR.
> The Tier 1 list is in [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md). Read it before your first task."

Point them to the full tier map: [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) and [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md).

> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`."

**Hard Rule #12:**
> "If requirements are unclear, Claude will ask one clarifying question at a time and wait.
> If you're prompting Claude and it asks a question, answer it before sending the next instruction."

**Contact map:**
Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) contact map section. Tell them:
> "Design tokens → UI Designer (#design-system). Commerce hooks → Integration Lead (#integration).
> Checkout / cart → Squad A Lead. PDP / search / account → Squad B Lead."

> `overrides/app/components/promo-code/`, and `overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/`.
> Before touching the header, footer, or shared product components, message Squad B Lead."

**Squad B (PDP, PLP, search, account):**
> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, `overrides/app/pages/product-list/`,
> `overrides/app/pages/account/`, and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`.
> Before touching checkout or cart components, message Squad A Lead."

- [/session-start](../session-start/SKILL.md) — run at the start of every session (mandatory)
- [/feature-spec](../feature-spec/SKILL.md) — before starting any non-trivial implementation
- [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) — before opening a PR
- [/pr-checklist](../pr-checklist/SKILL.md) — to generate PR description
- [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) — when you need E2E test coverage for a user journey

### First task

> "Your first task: read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) and [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) end to end.

### Testing layers

> Add `# DELTA:` and bring it to the next standup for classification."

### BrowserStack and Zephyr

> "BrowserStack cross-browser runs trigger automatically on PRs to `release/**`.
> Results link to your Zephyr stories via BrowserStack Test Observability.
> Check with the delivery lead that your Jira account has access to the BrowserStack project."

### First task

> "Your first task: read the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page end to end.
> Then review the reference `.feature` file under `e2e/features/checkout/`. If you spot anything that reads like a technical implementation detail rather than plain English, that's exactly the kind of thing to flag in an annotation."

name: project-init
description: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
---

This skill has five phases. Do not skip ahead — the script output in Phase 1 determines
which phases are needed and in what order.

---

## Phase 1 — Run the state detector

Run the check script:
```bash
bash scripts/projectInitCheck.sh
```

Read the output carefully. Note every [FAIL], [WARN], and [TODO] item.

Say to the developer:
> "Here's the current project setup status. I'll work through the issues in order."

---

## Phase 2 — Fix automatable failures

For each [FAIL] item in the script output, in priority order:

**Git hooks missing:**
Propose both commands together (they're always installed as a pair):
```bash
cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
```
Ask for confirmation before running. After running, verify with:
```bash
ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'
```

**Claude Code not installed:**
Provide the install command — do not run it yourself:
> "Run: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`"

**GitHub CLI not installed:**
> "Install `gh` from https://cli.github.com/ — needed for branch protection setup in Phase 4."

**Other FAIL items:** Provide the fix command, ask for confirmation, run it.

After addressing all [FAIL] items, re-run `scripts/projectInitCheck.sh` and confirm PASS count improved.

---

## Phase 3 — Human-input items

Work through [TODO] and [WARN] items one at a time. Ask one question, wait for the answer, update the relevant files, then ask the next.

**Tracking setup status:** Setup status is tracked on the [7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530) Confluence page (space `SFCC`, page ID `305430530`), not in a repo file. - Mark ✅ on the 7.1c Confluence page (see "Tracking setup status" above)

**Upstream baseline (if WARN: UNSET)**

When answered: Update [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) with the current version. Mark ✅ in checklist.

**BrowserStack account**
> "Has a BrowserStack account been set up for this project? Have BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME and BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY been added to GitHub Secrets?"

If yes: Mark ✅ in checklist. If no: Note who to contact (DevOps / Delivery Lead) and mark ⬜.

**QA test account credentials**
> "Have PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL and PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD been added to GitHub Secrets? These are the credentials for the registered test account in the SIT environment."

**E2E product SKUs**

Mark accordingly.

**Zephyr integration**
> "Which Zephyr product does the team use — Zephyr Scale (Cloud) or Zephyr Squad? This determines how BrowserStack Test Observability syncs results."

When answered: Update the comment in `.browserstack.yml` to name the correct product. Mark ✅ in checklist.

**LHCI secrets**
> "Have LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL, LHCI_TOKEN, and LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT been added to GitHub Secrets? These power the Lighthouse CI trend server."

Mark accordingly.

**MuleSoft contract endpoint**

Mark accordingly.

**GitHub Pages**
> "Has GitHub Pages been enabled? Settings → Pages → source: GitHub Actions. This is required for Playwright report publishing on develop pushes."

Mark accordingly.

---

## Phase 4 — Branch protection setup

If `gh` is installed and the developer is ready to configure branch protection:

> "Would you like me to set up release/** branch protection now? This requires admin access to the repo."

If yes, propose this command for the developer to confirm and run:

gh api repos/{OWNER}/{REPO}/branches/release%2F*/protection \

Re-read the [7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530) Confluence page (via `confluence_get_page`) and confirm the current state of all items.

- Never push to `develop` or `main`
- For items that require infrastructure (BrowserStack, LHCI server, MuleSoft), note the owner and move on — do not block the session on them
- If this is a re-run (some items already ✅), skip confirmed items and focus only on what remains ⬜

=== scripts/contentful/README.md ===
# Contentful tooling

Zimmermann uses **two different Contentful surfaces**. Keep them straight — they live in different places and are managed by different tools.

## 1. Content types (editorial schemas)

**What:** Schemas for editorial entries authors fill in (e.g. `shoppableImage`).
**Where:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — plain JS, one file per content type.
**How:** Push to the Contentful space via the Management API.

```bash
npm run sync:contentful
```

Driven by [sync.js](./sync.js). Reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, and `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` from `.env`. Upserts and publishes each content type.

To add a new content type: drop a new file in [content-types/](./content-types/) following the shape of [shoppableImage.js](./content-types/shoppableImage.js), then re-run the sync.

## 2. Studio Experiences component definitions (visual builder)

**What:** Registers Zimmermann React components with Contentful Studio Experiences so authors can drop them onto pages in the visual builder.
**Where:** Co-located with the React component — `overrides/app/components/<name>/<name>ContentfulDefinition.ts` (TypeScript, per the `overrides/` rule).
**How:** Imported at runtime by the `defineComponents` registry — no push step. Generated by the Claude skill below.

```
/contentful-register-component   # scaffold a new *ContentfulDefinition.ts
/contentful-drift-check          # diff React props vs the definition
```

Skills live in [.claude/skills/contentful-register-component/](../../.claude/skills/contentful-register-component/) and [.claude/skills/contentful-drift-check/](../../.claude/skills/contentful-drift-check/). The post-tool hook `contentfulDriftWarn.sh` flags when a `.tsx` component changes without its paired `*ContentfulDefinition.ts`.

# Upstream update policy

How we handle new releases of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` (and the surrounding PWA Kit SDKs).

## Principle

**Bump opportunistically — not on a schedule.** Stay on the current version unless a release contains something we actually care about.

Reasons to bump:
- **Security** — CVE fix, dependency patch with a known vulnerability, advisory we are exposed to.
- **SDK** — a change in `pwa-kit-runtime`, `pwa-kit-react-sdk`, `commerce-sdk-react`, or `pwa-kit-dev` that affects code we depend on (SSR, routing, hooks we use, build pipeline).
- **Bug fix or feature we have been waiting for** — a fix to behaviour we currently work around, or a feature that lets us delete custom code, or will help us on implementing a planned feature.

Reasons **not** to bump:
- A release with only template/UI changes that we have already overridden.
- A release whose changelog touches packages or paths we do not use.
- "It's been a while."

## Discipline

When the upstream-release-watch workflow opens a tracking issue (see [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml)):

1. Open the linked release notes.
2. Skim for the three categories above.
3. If nothing relevant, close the issue with a one-line reason and update `Reviewed up to` in [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](memory/upstreamBaseline.md). **Do not bump.**
4. If something relevant, bump — then update `Current` and `Reviewed up to` together.

## What we do not do

- **No drift detection script.** We do not diff our `overrides/` against the upstream template on a schedule. Drift is the *point* of the overrides pattern.
